title: Chat System
oneLine: Keep long-lived WebSockets at the edge, assign each conversation an ordered write path, persist messages before acknowledgement, and synchronize devices with cursors.
opening: I would use HTTP for account, history, and media APIs, and WebSockets for bidirectional real-time messaging and presence. A connection gateway authenticates the user and registers active devices with service discovery. A chat service routes each conversation to an owning partition/sequencer so message order is defined per conversation, assigns a server message ID, persists the message to a write-optimized store, and only then acknowledges acceptance. Delivery to online devices is asynchronous and at least once; clients deduplicate by message ID and send delivered/read acknowledgements. Offline devices catch up using a per-user or per-conversation cursor. Group membership is versioned, attachments go to object storage, and presence is soft state with heartbeat TTL rather than a strongly consistent database record.
ask: One-to-one, groups, or both—and maximum group size?
Which states are required: sent, delivered, read, typing, presence?
What ordering guarantee is required across conversations and devices?
How long is history retained and is end-to-end encryption required?
scale: Connection count and heartbeat traffic often dominate gateway capacity even when message QPS is moderate.
Ordering should normally be per conversation, not global; this enables partitioning.
Separate stored-message durability from online delivery attempts and ephemeral presence.

decisions.default: WebSocket for real-time messaging; HTTP for history/media/control.
decisions.why: WebSocket supports server push with fewer polling connections.
decisions.switch: Long polling for constrained environments; SSE for server-only streams.

decisions.default: Single ordered log/owner per conversation partition with stable message IDs.
decisions.why: Global ordering is expensive and unnecessary; client timestamps are untrusted.
decisions.switch: Large groups can split delivery fanout while preserving one ordered message log.

decisions.default: Persist-before-ack and at-least-once delivery with client/server dedupe.
decisions.why: Exactly-once network delivery is not realistic across disconnects and retries.
decisions.switch: Use transactional local state to make message creation exactly once within the service boundary.

decisions.default: Ephemeral TTL state and pub/sub, with privacy controls.
decisions.why: Presence changes rapidly and temporary staleness is acceptable.
decisions.switch: Store durable last-seen separately if product policy permits.

deepDives.title: Multi-device sync
points: Track a monotonic cursor per inbox/conversation.
A reconnect requests messages after the last acknowledged cursor.
Read state merges monotonically across devices and arrives out of order safely.

deepDives.title: Large groups
points: Persist one message, then fan out references/notifications.
Use membership version at send time and define semantics for concurrent joins/leaves.
Partition delivery workers and protect against whale groups.

deepDives.title: Connection draining
points: Mark gateway draining, stop new connections, update registry, and let clients reconnect with jitter.
Do not lose messages because delivery is replayed from durable storage.
Keep heartbeat intervals adaptive to mobile/network constraints.

failures.response: Client-generated idempotency ID plus server message ID; conditional creation returns existing result.
Connections re-establish elsewhere; durable messages sync from cursor; device registry expires by TTL.
Per-conversation sequence IDs, client buffering/gap detection, and history fetch for missing range.
Asynchronous partitioned delivery, bounded notification policy, and dedicated handling for whale groups.

questions.q: How do you guarantee message ordering?
questions.a: Define it per conversation, route writes through one logical sequencer/leader for that conversation, and assign server sequence IDs. Delivery can be parallel as long as clients reorder/detect gaps.

questions.q: How do read receipts work with multiple devices?
questions.a: Store a monotonic read cursor per user/conversation—the maximum message sequence seen. Device updates are idempotent max operations, then propagated asynchronously.
Clients upload through presigned URLs to object storage; the chat message contains immutable metadata and object reference. Scan/process asynchronously before broad delivery.

questions.q: How would end-to-end encryption change the design?
questions.a: Servers route encrypted envelopes and cannot inspect content for search/moderation. Key distribution, device identity, group key rotation, backup, and abuse-reporting become central design problems.

mistakes: Using presence as authoritative security state
seniorSignal: Separate durable creation, real-time delivery, device synchronization, and ephemeral presence. Be precise about the scope of ordering and acknowledgement semantics.
implementation: Netty/Spring WebFlux or .NET async sockets for gateways
Kafka/Pulsar or a sharded log for conversation ordering
Cassandra/Scylla-style message store keyed by conversation and time
Redis TTL registry/presence; object storage for media
